aggressive_definition_excerpt: However, dietary gamma-tocopherol, the most commonly consumed form of vitamin E in the United States, was significantly inversely related to the risk of advanced prostate cancer (for highest versus lowest quintile: RR, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.56-0.84; Ptrend = 0.001).
study_design: Prospective cohort analysis in the NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study
cohort_total_n_excerpt: We prospectively examined the relations of supplemental vitamin E and dietary intakes of alpha-, beta-, gamma-, and delta- tocopherols to prostate cancer risk among 295,344 men, ages 50 to 71 years and cancer-free at enrollment in 1995 to 1996, in the NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study.
reason: The abstract analyzes both total incident prostate cancer and incident advanced prostate cancer among men who were cancer-free at enrollment.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Supplemental vitamin E intake was not related to prostate cancer risk (for >0-99, 100-199, 200-399, 400-799, and > or = 800 IU/d versus never use: RR, 0.97, 0.89, 1.03, 0.99, and 0.97 (95% CI, 0.87-1.07) respectively; Ptrend = 0.90).
estimate_classifications.reason: This estimate is for supplemental vitamin E and overall prostate cancer, not the separately reported advanced endpoint for dietary gamma-tocopherol.
